newsitem.title: JAPAN: FORECAST-Japan Feb money supply growth seen steady.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Japan Feb money supply growth seen steady.

text.p: Japan's money supply growth for February is expected to be have been steady or mildly lower compared with January, but the growth is likely to slow down in future months, analysts said on Friday.

Economists polled by Reuters forecast that year-on-year growth of Japan's broadly defined money supply average of M2 plus certificates of deposit (M2+CDs) would range from 3.0 to 3.3 percent in February.
"Money supply is highly unlikely to grow more than in January," said Kyohei Morita, an economist at Nomura Research Institute.
In January, M2+CDs, Japan's key gauge of money supply, grew a preliminary 3.1 percent from a year earlier.
Morita said money supply was not expected to grow sharply longer term because many banks would be limiting their loans to the private sector.

"Banks are likely to keep their loans as small as possible...this will be the trend," Morita said. "They will be looking to avoid risks ahead of the government's plan to implement its Big Bang reforms."
Other economists agreed, and forecast that year-on-year growth of M2+CD may fall below the 3.0 percent level soon.
"Growth of money supply (M2+CD) will be in a declining phase in the future. It could fall below the 3.0 percent level soon," said Mamoru Yamaguchi, an economist at Nikko Research Center Ltd.
"Individuals and corporations who have shifted their funds out of bank deposits into instruments such as MMF and foreign bonds, are not returning funds back to bank deposits."
The February money supply figures will be released by the Bank of Japan at 8.50 a.m. on Tuesday (2350 GMT Monday).
